subproblems.title: Area integrand J is smooth and uniformly Legendre-elliptic near P = 0
subproblems.statement:
For all n, l in N let L = L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm and J(P) := sqrt(det(I_n + G(P))), G(P)_{ab} :=

(the area integrand of the frozen parent statement). Then (i) J is C^infinity on L (ContDiff R (top : N∞)), and (ii) there is eps > 0 such that for every P in L with ||P|| <= eps and every Q in L, (1/2)||Q||^2 <= D^2J(P)[Q][Q], where D^2J(P)[Q][Q] = fderiv R (fderiv R J) P Q Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (P (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (P (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ)))))) ∧ ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ‖P‖ ≤ ε → ∀ Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, 1 / 2 * ‖Q‖ ^ 2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fun P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det ((1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + Matrix.of fun a b : Fin n => inner ℝ (P (EuclideanSpace.single a (1 : ℝ))) (P (EuclideanSpace.single b (1 : ℝ))))))) P Q Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 and the Notation paragraph of the parent proof (J smooth, J(P) = 1 + |P|^2/2 + O(|P|^4), hence D^2J(0)[Q,Q] = |Q|_HS^2, and Legendre ellipticity by continuity), with the computation written out. Notation: fix n, l. L = L(R^n, R^l) with operator norm; e_1..e_n the standard basis of R^n; G(P) in Mat_n(R), G(P)_{ab} =

; J(P) = sqrt(det(I + G(P))); D^2J(P)[Q][Q'] := fderiv R (fderiv R J) P Q Q'. 1. Positivity. G(P) is symmetric and for xi in R^n, xi^T G(P) xi = sum_{a,b} xi_a xi_b

= |P(sum_a xi_a e_a)|^2 >= 0. Hence xi^T (I + G(P)) xi >= |xi|^2 > 0 for xi != 0, so I + G(P) is positive definite and det(I + G(P)) > 0 (Mathlib Matrix.PosDef.det_pos). 2. Smoothness (assertion (i)). Each entry P ->

is the continuous bilinear inner product composed with the continuous linear maps P -> P e_a, P -> P e_b, hence C^infinity on L. So P -> I + G(P) is C^infinity into the finite-dimensional matrix space and D(P) := det(I + G(P)) is C^infinity (det is a polynomial in the entries). By step 1, D(P) > 0 for all P, and sqrt is C^infinity on (0, infinity); hence J = sqrt o D is C^infinity on L. 3. Quadratic part along lines. Fix Q in L, put S := G(Q) and tau := tr S = sum_a |Q e_a|^2. For s in R, det(I + sS) = 1 + s tau + s^2 r(s) with r a polynomial (Mathlib Matrix.det_one_add_smul). Put phi(s) := sqrt(1 + s tau + s^2 r(s)); phi is C^infinity near s = 0 (the radicand is 1 at s = 0), phi(0) = 1 and phi'(0) = tau/2. Since G(tQ) = t^2 S, we have J(tQ) = phi(t^2) for t near 0. Hence f(t) := J(tQ) satisfies f'(t) = 2t phi'(t^2) and f''(t) = 2 phi'(t^2) + 4 t^2 phi''(t^2) near 0, so f''(0) = 2 phi'(0) = tau. 4. Second derivative at 0. J is C^2, so by the chain rule along t -> tQ, f''(t) = D^2J(tQ)[Q][Q]; thus D^2J(0)[Q][Q] = sum_a |Q e_a|^2. 5. Comparison with the operator norm. For h = sum_a h_a e_a with |h| = 1, |Q h| <= sum_a |h_a| |Q e_a| <= (sum_a h_a^2)^{1/2} (sum_a |Q e_a|^2)^{1/2} = (sum_a |Q e_a|^2)^{1/2} (Cauchy-Schwarz). Taking the sup over h: ||Q||^2 <= sum_a |Q e_a|^2 = D^2J(0)[Q][Q]. 6. Continuity of D^2J in components. Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L and c_L > 0 with |pi_r(Q)| <= c_L ||Q|| for the coordinate functionals pi_r (Q = sum_r pi_r(Q) E_r; finite dimension). Since J is C^2, each P -> D^2J(P)[E_r][E_s] is continuous. Put err(P) := c_L^2 sum_{r,s} |D^2J(P)[E_r][E_s] - D^2J(0)[E_r][E_s]|; err is continuous with err(0) = 0 and, by bilinearity, |D^2J(P)[Q][Q'] - D^2J(0)[Q][Q']| <= err(P) ||Q|| ||Q'|| for all Q, Q'. (This avoids any norm on the space of bilinear forms.) Choose eps > 0 with err(P) <= 1/2 whenever ||P|| <= eps. 7. Conclusion (assertion (ii)). For ||P|| <= eps and Q in L: D^2J(P)[Q][Q] >= D^2J(0)[Q][Q] - err(P)||Q||^2 >= ||Q||^2 - (1/2)||Q||^2 = (1/2)||Q||^2, by steps 4-6. Together with step 2 this proves the statement. QED Lean note: step 6 needs continuity of P ↦ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) P E_r E_s. One route avoids the bilinear-form type: for J of class C^2, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) P Q' Q = fderiv ℝ (fun P' => fderiv ℝ J P' Q) P Q' (fderiv_clm_apply with the constant second argument Q, then simp; checked at the pin), and P' ↦ fderiv ℝ J P' Q is a C^∞ map L → ℝ, so P ↦ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) P E_r E_s is continuous. With `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3` Lean synthesizes AddCommGroup, Module ℝ, NormedAddCommGroup, NormedSpace ℝ and FiniteDimensional ℝ for it, and (d⁻¹ • (a (x + d • e) - a x)) P Q = d⁻¹ * (a (x + d • e) P Q - a x P Q) closes by simp. The alternative, used in the argument above wherever possible, is to work only with the scalar components x ↦ a x P Q (values a x E_r E_s on a basis E_1..E_N of L), which needs no structure on that type.

subproblems.title: C^{m+1} on an open set implies D^m is alpha-Hoelder on compact subsets
subproblems.statement: Let E1, E2 be real normed spaces, m in N, 0 < alpha <= 1, V an open subset of E1 and h : E1 -> E2 with ContDiffOn R (m+1) h V. Then for every compact K contained in V there is C such that ||D^m h(x) - D^m h(y)|| <= C ||x - y||^alpha for all x, y in K, where D^m h = iteratedFDeriv R m h.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (E₁ E₂ : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [NormedSpace ℝ E₁] [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [NormedSpace ℝ E₂] (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (h : E₁ → E₂) (V : Set E₁), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ (m + 1 : ℕ) h V → ∀ K : Set E₁, IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m h x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ m h y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 2(b) and 5 of the parent proof ('F is C^1 on the open set O, hence Lipschitz on a compact neighbourhood of each compact set, which gives an alpha-Hoelder bound (short distances by the Lipschitz bound, long distances by 2 sup|F|/delta^alpha)'), stated for D^m h.
1. Setup. Put g := iteratedFDeriv R m h. Since V is open, iteratedFDeriv R j h = iteratedFDerivWithin R j h V on V for j <= m+1 (iteratedFDerivWithin_of_isOpen). As h is C^{m+1} on V, g is differentiable on V and, by the linear isometry of iteratedFDeriv_succ_eq_comp_left, ||Dg(x)|| = ||iteratedFDeriv R (m+1) h x||; the latter is continuous on V (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_iteratedFDerivWithin). So g and x -> ||Dg(x)|| are continuous on V.
2. If K is empty take C = 0. Otherwise, for each z in K choose r_z > 0 with B(z, 2 r_z) contained in V and ||Dg|| <= L_z := ||Dg(z)|| + 1 on B(z, 2 r_z) (continuity at z). By the mean value inequality on the convex ball (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le), ||g(x) - g(y)|| <= L_z ||x - y|| for x, y in B(z, 2 r_z).
3. Compactness: choose z_1..z_N in K with K contained in the union of the B(z_i, r_{z_i}); put L* := max_i L_{z_i}, r* := min_i r_{z_i} > 0 and S := sup_{x in K} ||g(x)|| < infinity (g continuous on the compact K).
4. Lipschitz bound on K. Let x, y in K. If ||x - y|| < r*, then x is in some B(z_i, r_{z_i}) and y in B(z_i, r_{z_i} + r*), contained in B(z_i, 2 r_{z_i}), so ||g(x) - g(y)|| <= L* ||x - y||. If ||x - y|| >= r*, then ||g(x) - g(y)|| <= 2S <= (2S/r*) ||x - y||. Hence ||g(x) - g(y)|| <= L' ||x - y|| on K with L' := max(L*, 2S/r*).
5. Hoelder bound. Let D := max(1, sup_{x,y in K} ||x - y||) < infinity. For x, y in K, since 0 < alpha <= 1, ||x - y|| = ||x - y||^{1-alpha} ||x - y||^alpha <= D^{1-alpha} ||x - y||^alpha (both sides are 0 if x = y, as 0^alpha = 0). Therefore ||g(x) - g(y)|| <= C ||x - y||^alpha with C := L' D^{1-alpha}. QED

local Lipschitz bounds on balls by the mean value inequality
finite subcover; short distances by local Lipschitz, long distances by 2 sup ||g||

0. Tools. (T0) Every Hoelder or Lipschitz constant below may and will be taken >= 0 (replace C by max(C, 0)); this is used whenever such inequalities are multiplied or composed, e.g. C_h ||f(x) - f(y)||^alpha <= C_h (Lam_f ||x - y||)^alpha needs C_h >= 0 and the monotonicity of t -> t^alpha on [0, infinity) for alpha > 0. For j = 0 this says phi itself is Lipschitz on compacts, because ||D^0 phi(x) - D^0 phi(y)|| = ||phi(x) - phi(y)|| (iteratedFDeriv R 0 phi x is the 0-multilinear map with value phi(x); the identification is a linear isometry, cf. norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). (T2) Continuous maps are bounded on compact sets and send compact sets to compact sets. 1. Regularity class. As f maps U into V, f is C^m on U and h is C^m on V, the chain rule gives h o f C^m on U (ContDiffOn.comp). Since U is open, iteratedFDeriv and iteratedFDerivWithin U agree on U. Moreover f is continuous on U, so K' = f(K) is compact and contained in V.
2. Case m = 0. Then ||D^0(h o f)(x) - D^0(h o f)(y)|| = ||h(f(x)) - h(f(y))||, and similarly for f and h. Since m = 0, the disjunctive hypothesis gives (a) or (b):

   (b) h is C^1 on V. Then h is Lipschitz on K' with constant Lam_h (T1), and f is alpha-Hoelder on K with constant C_f (hypothesis on f). So ||h(f(x)) - h(f(y))|| <= Lam_h C_f ||x - y||^alpha.
3. Case m >= 1: Faa di Bruno. For x in U (Mathlib iteratedFDeriv_comp, FaaDiBruno.lean, via FormalMultilinearSeries.taylorComp):
   D^m(h o f)(x) = sum over c of T_c( D^{k(c)} h(f(x)) ; D^{i_1(c)} f(x), ..., D^{i_{k(c)}(c)} f(x) ),
   the sum running over the finitely many ordered partitions c of {0,...,m-1} into k(c) in {1,...,m} blocks of sizes i_j(c) >= 1 with sum_j i_j(c) = m. Here T_c (compAlongOrderedFinpartition) is multilinear in its k(c)+1 arguments and ||T_c(A; B_1,...,B_k)|| <= ||A|| prod_j ||B_j||.
4. Bounds on K. (a) D^j h (0 <= j <= m) is continuous on V, so ||D^j h|| <= S_h on K'; D^i f (0 <= i <= m) is continuous on U, so ||D^i f|| <= S_f on K (T2).
   (b) Inner factors: for 1 <= i <= m-1, f is C^{i+1} on U, so D^i f is Lipschitz on K (T1), hence alpha-Hoelder on K (T3); D^m f is alpha-Hoelder on K by hypothesis. So ||D^i f(x) - D^i f(y)|| <= C_1 ||x - y||^alpha for 1 <= i <= m.
   (c) Outer factors: f is C^1 on U (m >= 1), hence Lipschitz on K with constant Lam_f (T1). For 1 <= j <= m-1, h is C^{j+1} on V, so D^j h is Lipschitz on K' with constant Lam_j (T1) and ||D^j h(f(x)) - D^j h(f(y))|| <= Lam_j Lam_f ||x - y|| <= Lam_j Lam_f max(1, diam K)^{1-alpha} ||x - y||^alpha. For j = m, ||D^m h(f(x)) - D^m h(f(y))|| <= C_h ||f(x) - f(y)||^alpha <= C_h Lam_f^alpha ||x - y||^alpha. So ||D^j h(f(x)) - D^j h(f(y))|| <= C_2 ||x - y||^alpha for 1 <= j <= m.
   (d) Order 0 (only needed if one uses the Mathlib lemma below, whose hypotheses range over all k <= m): ||f(x) - f(y)|| <= Lam_f ||x - y|| and ||h(f(x)) - h(f(y))|| <= Lam_0 Lam_f ||x - y|| with Lam_0 a Lipschitz constant of h on K' (T1, h is C^1 on V since m >= 1), hence both are alpha-Hoelder on K (T3); ||f|| <= S_f and ||h o f|| <= S_h on K.
5. Telescoping. For T as in step 3: T(A; B) - T(A'; B') = T(A - A'; B) + sum_{j=1}^{k} T(A'; B'_1,...,B'_{j-1}, B_j - B'_j, B_{j+1},...,B_k), hence ||T(A; B) - T(A'; B')|| <= ||A - A'|| prod_j ||B_j|| + ||A'|| sum_j ||B_j - B'_j|| prod_{i != j} max(||B_i||, ||B'_i||). With A = D^{k(c)}h(f(x)), A' = D^{k(c)}h(f(y)), B_j = D^{i_j(c)}f(x), B'_j = D^{i_j(c)}f(y), step 4 gives ||term_c(x) - term_c(y)|| <= (C_2 S_f^{k(c)} + S_h k(c) C_1 S_f^{k(c)-1}) ||x - y||^alpha.
6. Summing over the finitely many c gives ||D^m(h o f)(x) - D^m(h o f)(y)|| <= C ||x - y||^alpha on K. (Steps 5-6 are exactly Mathlib's FormalMultilinearSeries.taylorComp_sub_taylorComp_isBigO applied along the principal filter of K x K with comparison function (x, y) -> ||x - y||^alpha, which yields a uniform constant.) With step 1 both conjuncts hold. QED
Lean note: Mathlib already proves the pointwise analogue of steps 3-6, ContDiffPointwiseHolderAt.comp_of_differentiableAt (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiffHolder/Pointwise.lean, line 158 at the pin): it rewrites both iterated derivatives with iteratedFDeriv_comp (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/Comp.lean) and concludes with FormalMultilinearSeries.taylorComp_sub_taylorComp_isBigO (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiff/FaaDiBruno.lean, line 917). The same proof works for the uniform statement here: replace the filter 𝓝 a by the principal filter 𝓟 (K ×ˢ K) on pairs (x, y), with p₁ (x, y) = ftaylorSeries ℝ h (f x), p₂ (x, y) = ftaylorSeries ℝ h (f y), q₁ (x, y) = ftaylorSeries ℝ f x, q₂ (x, y) = ftaylorSeries ℝ f y and comparison function (x, y) ↦ ‖x - y‖ ^ α. On open sets iteratedFDeriv agrees with iteratedFDerivWithin (iteratedFDerivWithin_of_isOpen), so iteratedFDeriv_comp applies at every point of U. Asymptotics.isBigO_principal turns the resulting IsBigO into one uniform constant on K × K.

subproblems.title: Bilinear products preserve C^{m,alpha}_loc
subproblems.statement: Let E1, E2, E3, E4 be real normed spaces, m in N, 0 < alpha <= 1, B : E2 ->L E3 ->L E4 continuous bilinear, U open in E1, f : E1 -> E2 and g : E1 -> E3 both C^m on U with D^m f and D^m g alpha-Hoelder on every compact subset of U. Then x -> B(f x)(g x) is C^m on U and its m-th derivative is alpha-Hoelder on every compact subset of U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (E₁ E₂ E₃ E₄ : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [NormedSpace ℝ E₁] [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [NormedSpace ℝ E₂] [NormedAddCommGroup E₃] [NormedSpace ℝ E₃] [NormedAddCommGroup E₄] [NormedSpace ℝ E₄] (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (B : E₂ →L[ℝ] E₃ →L[ℝ] E₄) (f : E₁ → E₂) (g : E₁ → E₃) (U : Set E₁), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ m f U → (∀ K : Set E₁, IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m f x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ m f y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → ContDiffOn ℝ m g U → (∀ K : Set E₁, IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m g x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ m g y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → ContDiffOn ℝ m (fun x => B (f x) (g x)) U ∧ ∀ K : Set E₁, IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (fun x => B (f x) (g x)) x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (fun x => B (f x) (g x)) y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof ('products of C^{m,alpha}_loc functions are C^{m,alpha}_loc') and Step 2(c) for m = 0, reduced to the composition lemma.
1. The map beta : E2 x E3 -> E4, beta(y, z) := B y z, is a bounded bilinear map, hence C^infinity (IsBoundedBilinearMap.contDiff). In particular beta is C^1 and C^m on univ (an open set), and by the sibling dohr_eb_holder_of_contDiffOn_succ (with V = univ, beta being C^{m+1}) D^m beta is alpha-Hoelder on every compact subset of E2 x E3.
2. The pair p(x) := (f(x), g(x)) is C^m on U (ContDiffOn.prodMk). For x in U (U open, so f and g are C^m at x), D^m p(x) = (D^m f(x)).prod (D^m g(x)) (Mathlib iteratedFDeriv_prodMk), and the norm of such a product of multilinear maps is the max of the norms (ContinuousMultilinearMap.opNorm_prod). Hence for a compact K contained in U and x, y in K: ||D^m p(x) - D^m p(y)|| = max(||D^m f(x) - D^m f(y)||, ||D^m g(x) - D^m g(y)||) <= max(C_f, C_g) ||x - y||^alpha, with C_f, C_g the Hoelder constants of D^m f, D^m g on K.
3. Apply the sibling dohr_eb_holder_comp with the spaces E1, E2 x E3, E4, inner map p, outer map beta, open sets U and V := univ (p maps U into univ), and the alternative 'outer map C^1 on V' of its disjunctive hypothesis (valid for every m, including m = 0). It gives: beta o p is C^m on U and D^m(beta o p) is alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset of U. Since beta o p = (x -> B (f x) (g x)), both conjuncts follow. QED
proof_key_steps: beta(y, z) = B y z is smooth, hence C^{m,alpha}_loc on E2 x E3
the pair (f, g) is C^{m,alpha}_loc: D^m of a pair is the product, norm = max
apply holder_comp with the C^1 outer map beta

subproblems.title: C^{m+1,alpha}_loc iff the derivative (equivalently all partial derivatives) is C^{m,alpha}_loc
subproblems.statement: Let n, m in N, alpha in R, E a real normed space, U open in R^n and f : R^n -> E. Let (A) be: f is C^{m+1} on U and D^{m+1} f is alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset of U. Let (B) be: f is C^1 on U, Df is C^m on U and D^m(Df) is alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset of U. Let (C) be: f is C^1 on U and for every k in Fin n the partial derivative D_k f := (x -> Df(x) e_k) is C^m on U with D^m(D_k f) alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset of U. Then (A <-> B) and (A <-> C).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (m : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (f : Rn n → E) (U : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen U → (((ContDiffOn ℝ (m + 1 : ℕ) f U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (m + 1) f x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ (m + 1) f y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) ↔ (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ m (fderiv ℝ f) U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (fderiv ℝ f) x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (fderiv ℝ f) y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α)) ∧ ((ContDiffOn ℝ (m + 1 : ℕ) f U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ (m + 1) f x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ (m + 1) f y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) ↔ (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U ∧ ∀ k : Fin n, ContDiffOn ℝ m (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k (1 : ℝ))) U ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ y ∈ K, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (fun z => fderiv ℝ f z (EuclideanSpace.single k (1 : ℝ))) x - iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (fun z => fderiv ℝ f z (EuclideanSpace.single k (1 : ℝ))) y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the bookkeeping 'u in C^{m+1,alpha}_loc means Du in C^{m,alpha}_loc', 'v = D_k u ... for every direction k, i.e. u in C^{m+2,alpha}_loc' used in Steps 4-5 of the parent proof.
1. C^k part. On the open set U, ContDiffOn R (m+1) f U is equivalent to (DifferentiableOn R f U and ContDiffOn R m (fderiv R f) U) (contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen; the analyticity clause is vacuous for finite m). Since 1 <= m+1, ContDiffOn (m+1) implies C^1; and C^1 implies DifferentiableOn. Since R^n is finite-dimensional, ContDiffOn R m (fderiv R f) U holds iff for every v the map x -> Df(x) v is C^m on U (contDiffOn_clm_apply); by linearity in v it suffices to take v in {e_1,...,e_n}, because Df(x) = sum_k iota_k(D_k f(x)) where iota_k : E ->L L(R^n, E), iota_k(w) := (h -> <e_k, h> w), is a fixed continuous linear map, so Df is C^m whenever all D_k f are.
2. Isometry between D^{m+1} f and D^m(Df). For every x, iteratedFDeriv R (m+1) f x = Psi(iteratedFDeriv R m (fderiv R f) x) where Psi is a linear isometric equivalence (Mathlib iteratedFDeriv_succ_eq_comp_right, valid for all x). Hence ||D^{m+1}f(x) - D^{m+1}f(y)|| = ||D^m(Df)(x) - D^m(Df)(y)|| for all x, y, so the Hoelder clauses of (A) and (B) are literally equivalent (same constants). With step 1 this proves (A <-> B).
3. Components. Let ev_k : L(R^n, E) ->L E, T -> T e_k (norm <= 1). On the open set U, wherever Df is C^m: D^m(D_k f)(x) = ev_k o D^m(Df)(x) (iteratedFDeriv of a continuous linear map composed with a C^m map, ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_left with iteratedFDerivWithin_of_isOpen), so ||D^m(D_k f)(x) - D^m(D_k f)(y)|| <= ||D^m(Df)(x) - D^m(Df)(y)||. Conversely, wherever all D_k f are C^m: D^m(Df)(x) = sum_k iota_k o D^m(D_k f)(x) (iteratedFDeriv of a finite sum and of continuous linear images; ||iota_k|| <= 1), so ||D^m(Df)(x) - D^m(Df)(y)|| <= sum_k ||D^m(D_k f)(x) - D^m(D_k f)(y)||.
4. (B -> C): by step 1 each D_k f is C^m on U; for a compact K the constant of (B) works for every D_k f by step 3. (C -> B): Df is C^m on U by step 1, and for a compact K the sum over k of the constants of the D_k f works by step 3. Hence (B <-> C), and with step 2, (A <-> C). (For n = 0 all sums are empty and Df = 0; the argument is unchanged.) QED
proof_key_steps: contDiffOn_succ_iff_fderiv_of_isOpen and contDiffOn_clm_apply for the C^k parts
iteratedFDeriv (m+1) f = linear isometry applied to iteratedFDeriv m (fderiv f)
D^m(D_k f) = ev_k o D^m(Df) and D^m(Df) = sum_k iota_k o D^m(D_k f)
transfer of Hoelder constants in both directions

subproblems.title: Local C^{j,alpha} on a ball gives global C^{j,alpha} (IsHolderCkα) on the half ball
subproblems.statement: For m, k, j in N, alpha in R, u : R^m -> R^k, x0 in R^m and r in R: if IsLocallyHolderCkα j alpha u (ball x0 r) then IsHolderCkα j alpha u (ball x0 (r/2)), i.e. u is C^j on the half ball, all derivatives of order <= j are bounded there by one constant, and D^j u is alpha-Hoelder there with one constant.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m k j : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (u : Rn m → Rn k) (x₀ : Rn m) (r : ℝ), IsLocallyHolderCkα j α u (ball x₀ r) → IsHolderCkα j α u (ball x₀ (r / 2))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof ('each D^i u (i <= q+2) is continuous on the compact closed ball, hence bounded there; D^{q+2} u is alpha-Hoelder on the compact closed ball, hence on the open ball').
1. If r <= 0 then ball x0 (r/2) is empty and the three conditions of IsHolderCkα hold vacuously (ContDiffOn on the empty set; take B = 0 and K = 0). Assume r > 0.
2. ContDiffOn: ball x0 (r/2) is contained in ball x0 r, so ContDiffOn R j u (ball x0 (r/2)) follows from the first component of the hypothesis by monotonicity.
3. Bounds: K := closedBall x0 (r/2) is compact (proper space) and contained in ball x0 r since r/2 < r. As ball x0 r is open and u is C^j on it, for each i <= j the map iteratedFDeriv R i u is continuous on ball x0 r (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_iteratedFDerivWithin together with iteratedFDerivWithin_of_isOpen), hence bounded on K by some B_i. Put B := max_{i <= j} B_i; then ||iteratedFDeriv R i u x|| <= B for all i <= j and x in ball x0 (r/2), which is contained in K.
4. Hoelder: the second component of IsLocallyHolderCkα j alpha u (ball x0 r), applied to the compact K contained in ball x0 r, gives C with ||D^j u(x) - D^j u(y)|| <= C ||x - y||^alpha for x, y in K, in particular for x, y in ball x0 (r/2). Take this C as the constant in the third component of IsHolderCkα. QED

closedBall x0 (r/2) is a compact subset of ball x0 r
continuity of iteratedFDeriv i u on the open ball gives uniform bounds
Hoelder constant from the local hypothesis on the compact closed half ball

subproblems.title: Interior C^{1,alpha} Schauder estimate for C^{1,alpha} weak solutions of Legendre-elliptic divergence-form systems
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l in N, 0 < alpha < 1, lam > 0, M in R, R > 0, and L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm. There is a constant C such that for every x0 in R^n, every map a from R^n to continuous bilinear forms on L, every map Phi from R^n to continuous linear forms on L and every w : R^n -> R^l satisfying, on the open ball B := B_R(x0): (H1) lam ||P||^2 <= a(x)[P][P]; (H2) |a(x)[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||; (H3) |a(x)[P][Q] - a(y)[P][Q]| <= M |x - y|^alpha ||P|| ||Q||; (H4) |Phi(x)[P] - Phi(y)[P]| <= M |x - y|^alpha ||P||; (H5) |w(x)| <= M; (H6) w is C^1 on B; (H7) Dw is alpha-Hoelder on B with some (unquantified) constant; (H8) the integral over B of a(x)[Dw(x)][Dzeta(x)] equals the integral over B of Phi(x)[Dzeta(x)] for every C^1 compactly supported zeta : R^n -> R^l with tsupport in B; one has ||Dw(x)|| <= C and ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= C |x - y|^alpha for all x, y in B_{R/2}(x0). C depends only on n, l, alpha, lam, M, R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → α < 1 → ∀ lam M R : ℝ, 0 < lam → 0 < R → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (x₀ : Rn n) (a : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (Φ : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) (w : Rn n → Rn ℓ), (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, lam * ‖P‖ ^ 2 ≤ a x P P) → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |a x P Q| ≤ M * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ y ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ P Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |a x P Q - a y P Q| ≤ M * ‖x - y‖ ^ α * ‖P‖ * ‖Q‖) → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ y ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, |Φ x P - Φ y P| ≤ M * ‖x - y‖ ^ α * ‖P‖) → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ R, ‖w x‖ ≤ M) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 w (ball x₀ R) → (∃ K : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ ball x₀ R, ∀ y ∈ ball x₀ R, ‖fderiv ℝ w x - fderiv ℝ w y‖ ≤ K * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → (∀ ζ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → tsupport ζ ⊆ ball x₀ R → ∫ x in ball x₀ R, a x (fderiv ℝ w x) (fderiv ℝ ζ x) = ∫ x in ball x₀ R, Φ x (fderiv ℝ ζ x)) → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ (R / 2), ‖fderiv ℝ w x‖ ≤ C) ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball x₀ (R / 2), ∀ y ∈ ball x₀ (R / 2), ‖fderiv ℝ w x - fderiv ℝ w y‖ ≤ C * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is the Schauder step that the parent proof cites from Giaquinta-Martinazzi [GM] Theorems 5.17/5.19 (Hoelder coefficients satisfying (3.17), data in C^{0,sigma}, sigma = alpha). For C^{1,alpha} solutions it is proved here by L. Simon's blow-up method (L. Simon, Schauder estimates by scaling, Calc. Var. PDE 5 (1997) 391-407; the scalar divergence-form case is written out in S. Vita, Notes on Schauder estimates by scaling for elliptic PDEs in divergence form, arXiv:2510.01765, La Matematica 5 (2026)). Below, the Caccioppoli inequality (step 3) and the Liouville theorem (step 4) are proved directly for systems; the Legendre condition is what lets the scalar arguments go through unchanged. The method needs no Sobolev spaces: Caccioppoli, a Liouville theorem, Arzela-Ascoli and an absorption argument.
Notation. L = L(R^n, R^l), operator norm ||.||. For v in R^l, p in R^n, v (x) p in L is h -> <p, h> v, with ||v (x) p|| = |v| |p|. B_r(y) is the open ball. For a set A and a map F on A, [F]_{alpha;A} := sup{ ||F(x) - F(y)|| / |x - y|^alpha : x != y in A } in [0, infinity]; for Phi with values in linear forms, [Phi]_{alpha;A} := sup{ |Phi(x)[P] - Phi(y)[P]| / |x - y|^alpha : x != y in A, ||P|| <= 1 }. 'w is a weak solution of (a, Phi) on an open Omega' means: integral of a[Dw][Dzeta] = integral of Phi[Dzeta] for all zeta in C^1_c(R^n; R^l) with tsupport in Omega. Integrals of integrands supported in a compact subset of Omega may be taken over R^n.
0. Trivial case. If M < 0, (H5) fails at x0, so any C works. Assume M >= 0.
1. Two elementary facts. (1a) For zeta in C^1_c(R^n; R^l) and a fixed linear form c on L, the integral of c[Dzeta] over R^n is 0: c[Dzeta] = sum_{i,b} c[e_i (x) e_b] d_b zeta^i, and each d_b zeta^i integrates to 0 by Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on lines parallel to e_b (compact support). (1b) Interpolation: if w is C^1 on B_rho(x), e is a unit vector and 0 < t < rho, then w(x + te) - w(x) = t Dw(x)e + integral_0^t (Dw(x + se) - Dw(x)) e ds, hence |Dw(x)e| <= 2 sup_{B_rho(x)} |w| / t + t^alpha [Dw]_{alpha;B_rho(x)}, and taking the sup over e, ||Dw(x)|| <= 2 sup_{B_rho(x)} |w| / t + t^alpha [Dw]_{alpha;B_rho(x)}.
2. Scaling. Let (a, Phi, w) satisfy (H6)-(H8) on an open ball B_R'(x0') and let B_rho(y) be contained in B_R'(x0'). For z in B_1(0) put wt(z) := w(y + rho z), at(z) := a(y + rho z), Phit(z) := rho Phi(y + rho z). Then wt is C^1 on B_1, Dwt(z) = rho Dw(y + rho z), [Dwt]_{alpha;B_s(z0)} = rho^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho s}(y + rho z0)}, at satisfies (H1) with lam and (H2) with M, the Hoelder constant of at is rho^alpha times that of a, [Phit]_{alpha;B_1} = rho^{1+alpha} [Phi]_{alpha;B_rho(y)}, and wt is a weak solution of (at, Phit) on B_1: given zetat in C^1_c with tsupport in B_1, put zeta(x) := zetat((x - y)/rho), so tsupport zeta lies in B_rho(y), Dzeta(x) = rho^{-1} Dzetat((x - y)/rho), and the change of variables x = y + rho z (dx = rho^n dz) turns (H8) into rho^{n-2} integral at[Dwt][Dzetat] dz = rho^{n-2} integral Phit[Dzetat] dz.
3. Caccioppoli inequality for constant coefficients. Let A be a constant bilinear form on L with A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= Lam ||P|| ||Q||, and let V be C^1 on B_{2rho}(y) and a weak solution of (A, 0) there. Then for every c in R^l: integral over B_rho(y) of ||DV||^2 <= C3 rho^{-2} integral over B_{2rho}(y) of |V - c|^2, with C3 := 64 c_psi^2 Lam^2 / lam^2 (the right side may be infinite). Proof: fix once and for all psi in C^infinity(R) with 0 <= psi <= 1, psi = 1 on (-infinity, 1], psi = 0 on [3, infinity) (e.g. built from Real.smoothTransition), c_psi := sup |psi'|. Put eta(x) := psi(|x - y|^2 / rho^2): eta is C^infinity, eta = 1 on B_rho(y), tsupport eta lies in closedBall(y, sqrt(3) rho), contained in B_{2rho}(y), and |Deta| <= 2 sqrt(3) c_psi / rho <= 4 c_psi / rho. Test with zeta := eta^2 (V - c), which is C^1 with compact support in B_{2rho}(y): Dzeta = eta^2 DV + 2 eta (V - c) (x) Deta. Then 0 = integral A[DV][Dzeta] = integral eta^2 A[DV][DV] + 2 integral eta A[DV][(V - c) (x) Deta], so lam integral eta^2 ||DV||^2 <= 2 Lam integral eta ||DV|| |V - c| |Deta| <= (lam/2) integral eta^2 ||DV||^2 + (2 Lam^2 / lam) integral |V - c|^2 |Deta|^2 (Young). All integrals are finite (continuous integrands with compact support). Absorbing gives integral over B_rho(y) of ||DV||^2 <= integral eta^2 ||DV||^2 <= (4 Lam^2 / lam^2)(16 c_psi^2 / rho^2) integral over B_{2rho}(y) of |V - c|^2.
4. Liouville theorem. Let A be as in step 3 and let W be C^1 on R^n with [DW]_{alpha;R^n} <= Lam' < infinity (0 < alpha < 1) and W a weak solution of (A, 0) on R^n. Then DW is constant.
   4a. Mollification. Take phi in C^infinity_c(B_1(0)), phi >= 0, integral phi = 1 (normalized ContDiffBump), phi_eps(x) := eps^{-n} phi(x/eps), W_eps(x) := integral phi_eps(z) W(x - z) dz. W_eps is C^infinity (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left; W is continuous, hence locally integrable), DW_eps(x) = integral phi_eps(z) DW(x - z) dz (differentiation under the integral, DW continuous), so [DW_eps]_{alpha;R^n} <= Lam' and DW_eps(x) -> DW(x) as eps -> 0 for each x. W_eps is a weak solution: for zeta in C^1_c, by Fubini (continuous integrand with compact support in (x, z)) and the substitution x = x' + z, integral A[DW_eps(x)][Dzeta(x)] dx = integral phi_eps(z) (integral A[DW(x')][D(zeta(. + z))(x')] dx') dz = 0, since zeta(. + z) is an admissible test function.
   4b. Derivatives of smooth solutions are solutions. If V is C^infinity and a weak solution of (A, 0) on R^n, so is d_s V := DV(.) e_s: V_h := (V(. + h e_s) - V)/h is a weak solution (translate the test function: integral A[DV(x + h e_s)][Dzeta(x)] dx = integral A[DV(x)][Dzeta(x - h e_s)] dx = 0, and linearity), and DV_h -> D(d_s V) uniformly on tsupport zeta as h -> 0 (V is C^2; the limit of DV_h(x) is D^2V(x)[e_s][.], which equals D(d_s V)(x) = D^2V(x)[.][e_s] by symmetry of the second derivative of a C^2 map, ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt), so integral A[D(d_s V)][Dzeta] = lim integral A[DV_h][Dzeta] = 0. By induction every iterated partial derivative d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps is a weak solution.
   4c. Iterated Caccioppoli. For k >= 1 let Q_k(rho) := sum over (s_1..s_k) in {1..n}^k of integral over B_rho(0) of ||D(d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps)||^2. Claim: Q_k(rho) <= (n C3)^k rho^{-2k} integral over B_{2^k rho}(0) of ||DW_eps - P||^2 for every constant P in L and rho > 0. For k = 1: for each s, step 3 with V = d_s W_eps and c = P e_s gives integral over B_rho of ||D d_s W_eps||^2 <= C3 rho^{-2} integral over B_{2rho} of |d_s W_eps - P e_s|^2 <= C3 rho^{-2} integral over B_{2rho} of ||DW_eps - P||^2; sum over s. For k -> k+1: for each (s_0, s_1..s_k), step 3 with V = d_{s_0} d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps and c = 0 gives integral over B_rho of ||DV||^2 <= C3 rho^{-2} integral over B_{2rho} of |V|^2 <= C3 rho^{-2} integral over B_{2rho} of ||D(d_{s_1} ... d_{s_k} W_eps)||^2; summing over s_0 (factor n) and over (s_1..s_k): Q_{k+1}(rho) <= n C3 rho^{-2} Q_k(2rho) <= (n C3)^{k+1} rho^{-2(k+1)} integral over B_{2^{k+1} rho} of ||DW_eps - P||^2.
   4d. Vanishing of high derivatives. Take P := DW_eps(0) and k := n + 1. On B_{2^k rho}(0), ||DW_eps(x) - P|| <= Lam' |x|^alpha <= Lam' (2^k rho)^alpha, so Q_{n+1}(rho) <= c' rho^{n + 2 alpha - 2n - 2} = c' rho^{2 alpha - n - 2}, which tends to 0 as rho -> infinity. Q_{n+1} is nondecreasing in rho, hence identically 0, and every partial derivative of W_eps of order n + 2 vanishes identically (continuous, with zero L^2 norm on every ball).
   4e. Polynomial argument. Fix x in R^n and let p(t) := DW_eps(tx) - DW_eps(0), t in R, a C^infinity map into L. Its (n+1)-th derivative is D^{n+1}(DW_eps)(tx)[x,...,x] = 0 (all partials of order n + 2 vanish, i.e. the (n+2)-multilinear map D^{n+2}W_eps(y) vanishes on all tuples of basis vectors, hence is 0 by multilinearity), so p is a polynomial in t of degree <= n with p(0) = 0 (Taylor's formula with zero remainder, coordinatewise): p(t) = sum_{i=1}^{n} c_i t^i. Also ||p(t)|| <= Lam' |x|^alpha |t|^alpha. If some c_i != 0, let i0 be the largest such index; then ||p(t)|| / |t|^{i0} -> ||c_{i0}|| > 0 as t -> infinity, while ||p(t)|| / |t|^{i0} <= Lam' |x|^alpha |t|^{alpha - i0} -> 0 because i0 >= 1 > alpha; contradiction. So p = 0 and DW_eps(x) = DW_eps(0) for all x.
   4f. For all x, x': DW(x) - DW(x') = lim_{eps -> 0} (DW_eps(x) - DW_eps(x')) = 0. So DW is constant.
5. Key local estimate (blow-up). Claim: for every delta > 0 there is C_delta = C_delta(n, l, alpha, lam, M, delta) in N (in particular C_delta >= 0) such that, whenever at, Phit, wt on B_1 := B_1(0) satisfy (i) at[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2, |at[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q|| and |at(z)[P][Q] - at(z')[P][Q]| <= M |z - z'|^alpha ||P|| ||Q|| on B_1, (ii) wt is C^1 on B_1 with [Dwt]_{alpha;B_1} < infinity, (iii) wt is a weak solution of (at, Phit) on B_1, then [Dwt]_{alpha;B_{1/2}} <= delta [Dwt]_{alpha;B_1} + C_delta (sup_{B_1} |wt| + [Phit]_{alpha;B_1}).
   Proof by contradiction. If the claim fails for some delta > 0, then no k in N works as C_delta, i.e. for every k in N there are (a_k, Phi_k, w_k) satisfying (i)-(iii) with [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_{1/2}} > delta [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_1} + k (sup_{B_1}|w_k| + [Phi_k]_{alpha;B_1}). Then s_k := [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_{1/2}} lies in (0, infinity) (it is <= [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_1} < infinity). Replacing (w_k, Phi_k) by (w_k / s_k, Phi_k / s_k) (the equation is linear in (w, Phi); (i)-(iii) persist) we may assume [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_{1/2}} = 1, [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_1} < 1/delta, sup_{B_1}|w_k| < 1/k, [Phi_k]_{alpha;B_1} < 1/k.
   5a. Choose x_k != y_k in B_{1/2} with ||Dw_k(x_k) - Dw_k(y_k)|| >= (1/2)|x_k - y_k|^alpha and put rho_k := |x_k - y_k| in (0, 1).
   5b. For x in B_{1/2}, B_{1/2}(x) is contained in B_1, so (1b) with t in (0, 1/2) gives ||Dw_k(x)|| <= 2/(k t) + t^alpha / delta. With t = k^{-1/2} (k >= 5): eps_k := sup_{B_{1/2}} ||Dw_k|| <= 2 k^{-1/2} + k^{-alpha/2} / delta -> 0.
   5c. rho_k -> 0: otherwise for some sigma > 0 and infinitely many k, (1/2) sigma^alpha <= (1/2) rho_k^alpha <= ||Dw_k(x_k) - Dw_k(y_k)|| <= 2 eps_k -> 0, a contradiction. Discard finitely many k so that rho_k < 1/2.
   5d. Blow-up. For z in D_k := B_{1/(2 rho_k)}(0) (then x_k + rho_k z lies in B_{1/2}(x_k), contained in B_1) put W_k(z) := rho_k^{-1-alpha} [w_k(x_k + rho_k z) - w_k(x_k) - rho_k Dw_k(x_k) z]. Then W_k is C^1 on D_k, W_k(0) = 0, DW_k(z) = rho_k^{-alpha} [Dw_k(x_k + rho_k z) - Dw_k(x_k)], DW_k(0) = 0, [DW_k]_{alpha;D_k} <= [Dw_k]_{alpha;B_1} < 1/delta, hence ||DW_k(z)|| <= |z|^alpha / delta and |W_k(z)| <= |z|^{1+alpha} / delta on D_k (integrate along [0, z]). With e_k := (y_k - x_k)/rho_k (|e_k| = 1, e_k in D_k): ||DW_k(e_k)|| = rho_k^{-alpha} ||Dw_k(y_k) - Dw_k(x_k)|| >= 1/2.
   5e. Rescaled equation. Let A_k := a_k(x_k), P_k := Dw_k(x_k) (||P_k|| <= eps_k), ah_k(z) := a_k(x_k + rho_k z) and Psi_k(z) := rho_k^{-alpha} [Phi_k(x_k + rho_k z) - Phi_k(x_k)] - rho_k^{-alpha} [a_k(x_k + rho_k z) - a_k(x_k)][P_k] (a linear form on L). For zeta in C^1_c(R^n; R^l) with tsupport in D_k, test (iii) for w_k with zeta_k(x) := zeta((x - x_k)/rho_k) (tsupport in B_{1/2}(x_k), contained in B_1), change variables x = x_k + rho_k z, use Dw_k(x) = P_k + rho_k^alpha DW_k(z) and Dzeta_k(x) = rho_k^{-1} Dzeta(z), and subtract the vanishing integrals of A_k[P_k][Dzeta] and Phi_k(x_k)[Dzeta] (step 1a); after division by rho_k^{n-1+alpha}: integral ah_k(z)[DW_k(z)][Dzeta(z)] dz = integral Psi_k(z)[Dzeta(z)] dz. Bounds: |Psi_k(z)[P]| <= ([Phi_k]_{alpha;B_1} + M ||P_k||) |z|^alpha ||P|| <= (1/k + M eps_k) |z|^alpha ||P||, and |ah_k(z)[P][Q] - A_k[P][Q]| <= M rho_k^alpha |z|^alpha ||P|| ||Q||.
   5f. Compactness. The bilinear forms A_k satisfy |A_k[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||; in the finite-dimensional space of bilinear forms on L (e.g. via their components on a basis of L) a subsequence converges to some A, which satisfies A[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2 and |A[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||. Pass to a further subsequence with e_k -> e, |e| = 1. For each integer L0 >= 2 and k large (closedBall(0, L0) contained in D_k), the restrictions of W_k and DW_k to closedBall(0, L0) are uniformly bounded (by L0^{1+alpha}/delta and L0^alpha/delta) and equicontinuous (W_k is (L0^alpha/delta)-Lipschitz on the convex ball, DW_k is (1/delta, alpha)-Hoelder). By the Arzela-Ascoli theorem and a diagonal argument over L0 in N, a subsequence satisfies W_k -> W and DW_k -> V uniformly on compact subsets of R^n, with W, V continuous. Passing to the limit in W_k(z) - W_k(z') = integral_0^1 DW_k(z' + t(z - z'))(z - z') dt shows that W is C^1 with DW = V. Moreover [DW]_{alpha;R^n} <= 1/delta, DW(0) = 0, and ||DW(e)|| >= 1/2 because ||DW_k(e_k) - DW(e)|| <= |e_k - e|^alpha / delta + ||DW_k(e) - DW(e)|| -> 0.
   5g. Limit equation. For zeta in C^1_c with tsupport in B_{L0}(0) and k large: |integral ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta] - integral A[DW][Dzeta]| <= integral (|ah_k[DW_k][Dzeta] - A_k[DW_k][Dzeta]| + |(A_k - A)[DW_k][Dzeta]| + |A[DW_k - DW][Dzeta]|) -> 0 by the bounds of 5e-5f and uniform convergence on the compact support, and |integral Psi_k[Dzeta]| <= (1/k + M eps_k) L0^alpha integral ||Dzeta|| -> 0. Hence integral A[DW][Dzeta] = 0 for every zeta in C^1_c(R^n; R^l).
   5h. Step 4 (with Lam' = 1/delta, Lam = M) shows that DW is constant, so DW(e) = DW(0) = 0, contradicting ||DW(e)|| >= 1/2. This proves the claim.
6. Absorption on the unit ball. Let (a, Phi, w) satisfy (H1)-(H8) on B_1 := B_1(0) (i.e. x0 = 0, R = 1, constants lam, M). Put Gam := sup_{B_1} |w| + [Phi]_{alpha;B_1} <= 2M (by (H5), (H4)) and Q := sup{ rho^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/2}(y)} : y in B_1, 0 < rho <= 1 - |y| } (these are exactly the balls B_rho(y) contained in B_1). By (H7), Q <= [Dw]_{alpha;B_1} < infinity. Fix delta := 1/16 and let C_delta be the constant of step 5.
   6a. For every ball B_rho(y) contained in B_1 (so rho <= 1), step 2 (scaling to B_1: the scaled coefficient has Hoelder constant M rho^alpha <= M, the scaled Phi has [Phit]_{alpha;B_1} = rho^{1+alpha}[Phi]_{alpha;B_rho(y)} <= [Phi]_{alpha;B_1}, sup |wt| <= sup_{B_1} |w|, and [Dwt]_{alpha;B_1} < infinity) and step 5 give rho^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/2}(y)} <= delta rho^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_rho(y)} + C_delta Gam.
   6b. Fix a ball B_rho(y0) contained in B_1 and x in B_{rho/2}(y0). Then B_{rho/2}(x) is contained in B_rho(y0), hence in B_1, so by the definition of Q (radius rho/2, center x), (rho/2)^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/4}(x)} <= Q; and 6a with (x, rho/4) gives (rho/4)^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/8}(x)} <= delta (rho/4)^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/4}(x)} + C_delta Gam. Hence [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/8}(x)} <= H(rho) := delta (2/rho)^{1+alpha} Q + C_delta Gam (4/rho)^{1+alpha}.
   6c. Sup bound: for x in B_{rho/2}(y0), (1b) on B_{rho/8}(x) with t = rho/16 gives ||Dw(x)|| <= 32 Gam / rho + (rho/16)^alpha H(rho).
   6d. Hoelder bound on B_{rho/2}(y0): for x != y in B_{rho/2}(y0), if |x - y| < rho/8 then y is in B_{rho/8}(x) and ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= H(rho) |x - y|^alpha; if |x - y| >= rho/8 then ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= 2 sup_{B_{rho/2}(y0)} ||Dw|| <= 2 (8/rho)^alpha [32 Gam / rho + (rho/16)^alpha H(rho)] |x - y|^alpha. Since rho^{1+alpha} H(rho) = delta 2^{1+alpha} Q + C_delta 4^{1+alpha} Gam <= 4 delta Q + 16 C_delta Gam, multiplying by rho^{1+alpha} yields rho^{1+alpha} [Dw]_{alpha;B_{rho/2}(y0)} <= max(4 delta Q + 16 C_delta Gam, 64 * 8^alpha Gam + 2 * 2^{-alpha} (4 delta Q + 16 C_delta Gam)) <= 8 delta Q + (512 + 32 C_delta) Gam.
   6e. Taking the sup over (y0, rho): Q <= 8 delta Q + (512 + 32 C_delta) Gam = Q/2 + (512 + 32 C_delta) Gam (as delta = 1/16); since Q < infinity, Q <= (1024 + 64 C_delta) Gam <= (2048 + 128 C_delta) M.
   6f. With (y0, rho) = (0, 1): [Dw]_{alpha;B_{1/2}} <= Q and, by 6c, ||Dw(x)|| <= 32 Gam + H(1) <= 64 M + 4 delta Q + 32 C_delta M = 64 M + Q/4 + 32 C_delta M for x in B_{1/2}. So both conclusions hold on B_{1/2}(0) with a constant C_1 depending only on (n, l, alpha, lam, M).
7. General R and x0. Given data on B_R(x0), apply step 2 with (y, rho) := (x0, R): wt(z) = w(x0 + Rz), at(z) = a(x0 + Rz), Phit(z) = R Phi(x0 + Rz) satisfy (H1)-(H8) on B_1(0) with lam and M' := M max(1, R^alpha, R^{1+alpha}) (bounds: |at| <= M, Hoelder constant of at is M R^alpha, Hoelder constant of Phit is M R^{1+alpha}, |wt| <= M, and (H7) persists). Step 6 with M' gives C_1(M') with ||Dwt|| <= C_1 and [Dwt]_{alpha;B_{1/2}} <= C_1. Since Dw(x0 + Rz) = R^{-1} Dwt(z), for x, y in B_{R/2}(x0): ||Dw(x)|| <= C_1 / R and ||Dw(x) - Dw(y)|| <= R^{-1} C_1 |(x - y)/R|^alpha = R^{-1-alpha} C_1 |x - y|^alpha. Hence C := C_1(M') max(R^{-1}, R^{-1-alpha}) works; it depends only on n, l, alpha, lam, M, R. QED

subproblems.title: Uniform C^{1,alpha} bounds on difference quotients give a C^{1,alpha} directional derivative
subproblems.statement: Let n, l in N, 0 < alpha <= 1, f : R^n -> R^l, x0, e in R^n, rho, M in R and delta > 0, with f C^1 on B_{rho + delta|e|}(x0). Assume that for all real d with 0 < |d| < delta and all x, y in B_rho(x0): ||d^{-1}(Df(x + de) - Df(x))|| <= M and ||d^{-1}(Df(x + de) - Df(x)) - d^{-1}(Df(y + de) - Df(y))|| <= M |x - y|^alpha. Then the directional derivative D_e f := (x -> Df(x) e) is C^1 on B_rho(x0), ||D(D_e f)(x)|| <= M and ||D(D_e f)(x) - D(D_e f)(y)|| <= M |x - y|^alpha for x, y in B_rho(x0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (f : Rn n → Rn ℓ) (x₀ e : Rn n) (ρ δ M : ℝ), 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → 0 < δ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (ball x₀ (ρ + δ * ‖e‖)) → (∀ d : ℝ, d ≠ 0 → |d| < δ → ∀ x ∈ ball x₀ ρ, ‖d⁻¹ • (fderiv ℝ f (x + d • e) - fderiv ℝ f x)‖ ≤ M) → (∀ d : ℝ, d ≠ 0 → |d| < δ → ∀ x ∈ ball x₀ ρ, ∀ y ∈ ball x₀ ρ, ‖d⁻¹ • (fderiv ℝ f (x + d • e) - fderiv ℝ f x) - d⁻¹ • (fderiv ℝ f (y + d • e) - fderiv ℝ f y)‖ ≤ M * ‖x - y‖ ^ α) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x e) (ball x₀ ρ) ∧ (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ ρ, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ f z e) x‖ ≤ M) ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball x₀ ρ, ∀ y ∈ ball x₀ ρ, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ f z e) x - fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ f z e) y‖ ≤ M * ‖x - y‖ ^ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof (difference quotients w_d = (u(. + d e_k) - u)/d, uniform bounds in d, passage to the limit d -> 0 identifying D(D_k u) with the limit of D w_d; [GM] Section 4.3, Proposition 4.8). Here the uniform bounds are in C^{1,alpha} instead of W^{1,2}, and the limit is taken by uniform convergence instead of weak L^2 convergence.
Notation: B := B_rho(x0), B' := B_{rho + delta|e|}(x0) (open), g_d(x) := d^{-1}(f(x + de) - f(x)) for 0 < |d| < delta. If rho <= 0, B is empty and all conclusions are vacuous; assume rho > 0 (then the hypotheses force M >= 0).
1. For 0 < |d| < delta and x in B, x + de lies in B' (|x + de - x0| < rho + delta|e|). Hence g_d is C^1 on B with Dg_d(x) = d^{-1}(Df(x + de) - Df(x)) (chain rule, B' open), and by hypothesis ||Dg_d(x)|| <= M and ||Dg_d(x) - Dg_d(y)|| <= M |x - y|^alpha on B.
2. g_d -> D_e f uniformly on compact subsets K of B as d -> 0. Fix 0 < delta' < delta; K + closedBall(0, delta'|e|) is compact and contained in B'. For |d| < delta' and x in K, g_d(x) - Df(x)e = integral_0^1 (Df(x + t d e) - Df(x)) e dt (fundamental theorem of calculus on the segment, contained in B'), so ||g_d(x) - Df(x)e|| <= |e| sup{ ||Df(x') - Df(x)|| : x in K, |x' - x| <= |d||e| }, which tends to 0 as d -> 0 by uniform continuity of Df on that compact set.
3. Interpolation. Let x in B and r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) contained in B. For admissible d, d' put h := g_d - g_{d'}; h is C^1 on B with ||Dh(y) - Dh(y')|| <= 2M |y - y'|^alpha. For y in closedBall(x, r), a unit vector v and 0 < t <= r, the segment y + [0, t]v lies in closedBall(x, 2r) and h(y + tv) - h(y) = t Dh(y)v + integral_0^t (Dh(y + sv) - Dh(y)) v ds, so ||Dh(y)v|| <= 2S/t + 2M t^alpha with S := sup over closedBall(x, 2r) of ||g_d - g_{d'}||; taking the sup over v, ||Dh(y)|| <= 2S/t + 2M t^alpha.
4. Uniform Cauchy property. Given eta > 0 choose t in (0, r] with 2M t^alpha < eta/2, then (step 2 with K = closedBall(x, 2r)) d0 > 0 such that S < eta t / 4 whenever 0 < |d|, |d'| < d0. Then sup over closedBall(x, r) of ||Dg_d - Dg_{d'}|| < eta. Since L(R^n, R^l) is complete, there is V : B -> L(R^n, R^l) with Dg_d -> V uniformly on every such closedBall(x, r) as d -> 0 along the punctured neighbourhood filter of 0 (the limit is pointwise, hence independent of the ball).
5. Bounds for V. As pointwise limits of the bounds in step 1: ||V(y)|| <= M and ||V(y) - V(y')|| <= M |y - y'|^alpha for y, y' in B. In particular V is continuous on B.
6. Differentiability. On each open ball B_r(x) with closedBall(x, 2r) contained in B: each g_d is differentiable with derivative Dg_d, g_d -> D_e f pointwise (step 2) and Dg_d -> V uniformly (step 4). By the theorem on uniform limits of derivatives (Mathlib hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoUniformlyOn / hasFDerivAt_of_tendstoUniformlyOnFilter, along the punctured filter at 0 restricted to |d| < delta, which is not bottom), D_e f has derivative V(y) at every y in B_r(x). Every point of B lies in such a ball, so D_e f is differentiable on B with fderiv R (D_e f) y = V(y).
7. Conclusion. fderiv R (D_e f) = V is continuous on the open set B, so D_e f is C^1 on B; the bound ||fderiv R (D_e f) y|| <= M and the Hoelder estimate with constant M are step 5. QED

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3-4 of the parent proof (difference quotients of the system (E) as in [GM] Proposition 8.6, then the Schauder estimate of [GM] Theorem 5.19), in the classical form: the Schauder estimate (sibling dohr_eb_schauder_interior_estimate) is applied to the difference quotients themselves, uniformly in d, and the limit d -> 0 is taken with the sibling dohr_eb_difference_quotient_limit. This replaces the W^{2,2} detour of the parent Step 3 and needs no Sobolev spaces.
Notation: L = L(R^n, R^l), A(P) := DPsi(P) (a linear form on L), B(P) := D^2 Psi(P) (bilinear form, B(P)[Q][Q'] = fderiv R (fderiv R Psi) P Q Q'), e_k = EuclideanSpace.single k 1.
0. Preliminaries. IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha u U says: u is C^1 on U and Du is alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset of U, since ||iteratedFDeriv R 1 u x - iteratedFDeriv R 1 u y|| = ||Du(x) - Du(y)|| (linear isometry, iteratedFDeriv_one_apply / norm_iteratedFDeriv_one). IsLocallyHolderCkα 0 alpha g U says: g is continuous on U and alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset (||iteratedFDeriv R 0 g x - iteratedFDeriv R 0 g y|| = |g(x) - g(y)|). If U is empty the conclusion is trivial; otherwise eps >= 0.
1. Constants of Psi on Kc := closedBall(0, eps) in L (compact, convex). Psi is C^3, so the functions P -> B(P)[Q][Q'] are C^1. Let M_B := sup{ |B(P)[Q][Q']| : P in Kc, ||Q||, ||Q'|| <= 1 } < infinity, and let L_B be a constant with |B(P)[Q][Q'] - B(P')[Q][Q']| <= L_B ||P - P'|| ||Q|| ||Q'|| for P, P' in Kc (mean value inequality on the convex Kc for the C^1 functions P -> B(P)[E_r][E_s] on a basis E_r of L, plus bilinearity; this avoids norms on the space of bilinear forms).
2. Localization. Fix xb in U and R > 0 with closedBall(xb, 4R) contained in U; K0 := closedBall(xb, 4R) is compact. Let H1 be a Hoelder constant of Du on K0 and H2 one of g on K0. Fix k in {1,...,n}, e := e_k (|e| = 1), and for 0 < |d| < R put w_d(x) := d^{-1}(u(x + de) - u(x)).
3. For x in Bb := B_{2R}(xb), both x and x + de lie in B_{3R}(xb), contained in U. Hence w_d is C^1 on Bb, Dw_d(x) = d^{-1}(Du(x + de) - Du(x)), ||Dw_d(x) - Dw_d(y)|| <= 2 H1 |d|^{-1} |x - y|^alpha on Bb (qualitative Hoelder bound), and |w_d(x)| = |integral_0^1 Du(x + t d e) e dt| <= eps.
4. Linear system for w_d. For x in Bb let P_t(x) := Du(x) + t(Du(x + de) - Du(x)) (t in [0, 1]); P_t(x) lies in Kc as a convex combination of two points of Kc. Define the bilinear form a_d(x)[P][Q] := integral_0^1 B(P_t(x))[P][Q] dt (bilinear and continuous; as a Lean object it can be built with LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap from the L*-valued integral P -> integral_0^1 B(P_t(x))[P] dt), G_d(x) := integral_0^1 g(x + t d e) dt in R^l, and the linear form Phi_d(x)[P] := <G_d(x), P e>. Claim: for every zeta in C^1_c(R^n; R^l) with tsupport in Bb, integral over Bb of a_d(x)[Dw_d(x)][Dzeta(x)] = integral over Bb of Phi_d(x)[Dzeta(x)].
   (a) Test the hypothesis with phi1 := zeta(. - de) and phi2 := zeta (both C^1 with compact support and tsupport in B_{3R}(xb), contained in U). The integrands vanish outside tsupport phi (there phi = 0 and Dphi = 0), so all integrals may be taken over R^n. Translating x = y + de in the phi1-equation (translation invariance of Lebesgue measure): integral A(Du(y + de))[Dzeta(y)] dy = - integral <zeta(y), g(y + de)> dy. Subtracting the phi2-equation: integral [A(Du(y + de)) - A(Du(y))][Dzeta(y)] dy = - integral <zeta(y), g(y + de) - g(y)> dy.
   (b) For each y, A(Du(y + de)) - A(Du(y)) = integral_0^1 B(P_t(y))[Du(y + de) - Du(y)] dt (fundamental theorem of calculus for the C^1 map t -> A(P_t(y)), whose derivative is B(P_t(y))[Du(y + de) - Du(y)]) = d a_d(y)[Dw_d(y)]. So the left side equals d times integral a_d[Dw_d][Dzeta].
   (c) The right side equals, by translation, integral <zeta(x) - zeta(x - de), g(x)> dx, and zeta(x) - zeta(x - de) = d integral_0^1 Dzeta(x - t d e) e dt; by Fubini (continuous integrand with compact support in [0,1] x R^n) and the translation x = y + t d e this is d integral <G_d(y), Dzeta(y) e> dy = d integral Phi_d[Dzeta].
   (d) Divide by d != 0. (All integrands used in (a)-(c) are continuous on R^n with compact support even though g, Du need not be controlled outside U: each integrand vanishes on a neighbourhood of every point outside the relevant translate of tsupport zeta, which is a compact subset of U on which g and Du are continuous; this justifies the translations and Fubini.)
5. Uniform hypotheses of the sibling dohr_eb_schauder_interior_estimate on Bb = B_{2R}(xb), with constants independent of d and k: (H1) a_d(x)[P][P] = integral_0^1 B(P_t(x))[P][P] dt >= lam ||P||^2 (P_t(x) in Kc and the Legendre hypothesis); (H2) |a_d(x)[P][Q]| <= M_B ||P|| ||Q||; (H3) |a_d(x)[P][Q] - a_d(y)[P][Q]| <= L_B sup_t ||P_t(x) - P_t(y)|| ||P|| ||Q|| <= L_B H1 |x - y|^alpha ||P|| ||Q||, since ||P_t(x) - P_t(y)|| <= (1 - t)||Du(x) - Du(y)|| + t||Du(x + de) - Du(y + de)|| and all four points lie in K0; (H4) |Phi_d(x)[P] - Phi_d(y)[P]| <= |G_d(x) - G_d(y)| ||P|| <= H2 |x - y|^alpha ||P||; (H5) |w_d| <= eps; (H6), (H7) by step 3; (H8) by step 4. With M := max(M_B, L_B H1, H2, eps, 0), the sibling applied to (n, l, alpha, lam, M, 2R) gives C, independent of d and k, with ||Dw_d(x)|| <= C and ||Dw_d(x) - Dw_d(y)|| <= C |x - y|^alpha for x, y in B_R(xb) and all 0 < |d| < R.
6. Apply the sibling dohr_eb_difference_quotient_limit with f := u, x0 := xb, e := e_k, rho := R, delta := R, M := C: u is C^1 on B_{R + R|e|}(xb) = B_{2R}(xb), contained in U, and its two hypotheses are the bounds of step 5 because d^{-1}(Du(x + de) - Du(x)) = Dw_d(x). Hence v_k := (x -> Du(x) e_k) is C^1 on B_R(xb) with ||Dv_k|| <= C and ||Dv_k(x) - Dv_k(y)|| <= C |x - y|^alpha there.
7. Local to global. (a) Every point of U is the centre xb of such a ball, so v_k is C^1 on U (contDiffOn_of_locally_contDiffOn). (b) Let K be a compact subset of U. Cover K by the balls B_{R(xb)}(xb), xb in K, chosen as in step 2, take a finite subcover B_{R_i}(xb_i), i <= N, with constants C_i from step 6, and let C* := max_i C_i. By the Lebesgue number lemma (lebesgue_number_lemma_of_metric) there is eta > 0 such that for every x in K the ball B_eta(x) lies in some B_{R_i}(xb_i). For x, y in K: if |x - y| < eta, both lie in one B_{R_i}(xb_i) and ||Dv_k(x) - Dv_k(y)|| <= C* |x - y|^alpha; otherwise ||Dv_k(x) - Dv_k(y)|| <= 2C* <= 2C* eta^{-alpha} |x - y|^alpha. Since ||iteratedFDeriv R 1 v_k x - iteratedFDeriv R 1 v_k y|| = ||Dv_k(x) - Dv_k(y)||, IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha v_k U holds for every k.
8. Conclusion. u is C^1 on U and every v_k = (x -> fderiv R u x e_k) satisfies IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha v_k U; by the sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv (direction (C) => (A) with m = 1 and E = R^l, whose (A) is exactly IsLocallyHolderCkα 2 alpha u U), IsLocallyHolderCkα 2 alpha u U. QED

Then IsLocallyHolderCkα (m+1) alpha v U.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the parent proof's Step 5 cites [GM] Theorem 5.20 (coefficients and data in C^{k,sigma}_loc give v in C^{k+1,sigma}_loc), whose proof in [GM] is induction on k: differentiate the system and apply the order-(k-1) case, with Theorem 5.19 at the bottom. Here this is done classically: base case m = 1 by difference quotients plus the Schauder estimate (siblings dohr_eb_schauder_interior_estimate and dohr_eb_difference_quotient_limit), inductive step by differentiating the system.
Notation: L = L(R^n, R^l), e_s = EuclideanSpace.single s 1, D_s F(x) := DF(x) e_s. Fix a basis E_1..E_N of L with coordinate functionals pi_r (P = sum_r pi_r(P) E_r, |pi_r(P)| <= c_L ||P||). Write a_{rt}(x) := a(x)[E_r][E_t] and Phi_r(x) := Phi(x)[E_r]. The induction is on m, for all (U, lam, a, Phi, v) simultaneously.
P1 (components). If |a_{rt}| <= S and |a_{rt}(x) - a_{rt}(y)| <= H |x - y|^alpha for all r, t on a set A, then |a(x)[P][Q]| <= N^2 c_L^2 S ||P|| ||Q|| and |a(x)[P][Q] - a(y)[P][Q]| <= N^2 c_L^2 H |x - y|^alpha ||P|| ||Q|| on A, by bilinearity; similarly for Phi.
P2 (scalar Hoelder facts). If phi : R^n -> R is in C^{j,alpha}_loc(U) with j >= 1, then phi is C^1 on U, hence Lipschitz and alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset (sibling dohr_eb_holder_of_contDiffOn_succ with m = 0, using ||iteratedFDeriv R 0 phi x - iteratedFDeriv R 0 phi y|| = |phi(x) - phi(y)|); its derivatives of order <= j are continuous, hence bounded on compacts; and each D_s phi lies in C^{j-1,alpha}_loc(U) (sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv, (A) => (C), E = R). In particular for j = 1, D phi is alpha-Hoelder on compacts.
P3 (covering). If every point of U is the centre of a ball B_R(xb), contained in U, on which a function F is C^1 with ||DF|| <= C_xb and DF alpha-Hoelder with constant C_xb, then IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha F U (finite subcover of a compact K plus a Lebesgue number eta: pairs closer than eta lie in one ball, other pairs are handled by 2 max C_i <= 2 max C_i eta^{-alpha} |x - y|^alpha; and ||iteratedFDeriv R 1 F x - iteratedFDeriv R 1 F y|| = ||DF(x) - DF(y)||).
Base case m = 1.
1. Fix xb in U and R > 0 with K0 := closedBall(xb, 4R) contained in U, and k in {1..n}, e := e_k. On K0, by P2 and the hypotheses with m = 1: |a_{rt}| <= S_a, ||Da_{rt}|| <= S'_a, a_{rt} is alpha-Hoelder with H_a (Lipschitz on the convex K0), Da_{rt} is alpha-Hoelder with H'_a; ||DPhi_r|| <= S'_Phi and DPhi_r is alpha-Hoelder with H'_Phi; from IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha v U: v is C^1, ||Dv|| <= S_v and Dv is alpha-Hoelder with H_v on K0.
2. For 0 < |d| < R and x in Bb := B_{2R}(xb) put w_d(x) := d^{-1}(v(x + de) - v(x)); x + de lies in B_{3R}(xb), contained in U. Then w_d is C^1 on Bb, Dw_d(x) = d^{-1}(Dv(x + de) - Dv(x)), Dw_d is alpha-Hoelder on Bb with constant 2 H_v/|d| (qualitative), and |w_d| <= S_v (mean value).
3. Equation for w_d. For zeta in C^1_c with tsupport in Bb, test the hypothesis with zeta(. - de) and with zeta (tsupports in B_{3R}(xb), contained in U; integrands vanish outside the tsupports, so integrate over R^n), translate x = y + de in the first, subtract, use a(y + de)[Dv(y + de)] - a(y)[Dv(y)] = a(y)[Dv(y + de) - Dv(y)] + (a(y + de) - a(y))[Dv(y + de)], and divide by d (the integrands are continuous with compact support on R^n: they vanish on a neighbourhood of each point outside the compact translates of tsupport zeta, which lie in U where a, Phi, Dv are continuous). This gives integral over Bb of a(x)[Dw_d(x)][Dzeta(x)] = integral over Bb of Phi_d(x)[Dzeta(x)], with Phi_d(x)[P] := d^{-1}(Phi(x + de) - Phi(x))[P] - alpha_d(x)[Dv(x + de)][P] and alpha_d(x) := d^{-1}(a(x + de) - a(x)).
4. Uniform bounds on Bb (independent of d). (H1) Legendre with lam (hypothesis). (H2), (H3): by P1 with S_a and H_a. (H4): for each r, d^{-1}(Phi_r(x + de) - Phi_r(x)) = integral_0^1 DPhi_r(x + t d e) e dt has Hoelder constant <= H'_Phi on Bb; alpha_d(x)[E_r][E_t] = integral_0^1 Da_{rt}(x + t d e) e dt is bounded by S'_a and alpha-Hoelder with H'_a, so by P1 |alpha_d(x)[Q][P]| <= c S'_a ||Q|| ||P|| and |alpha_d(x)[Q][P] - alpha_d(y)[Q][P]| <= c H'_a |x - y|^alpha ||Q|| ||P||; with Q = Dv(x + de) (bounded by S_v, alpha-Hoelder with H_v) the product rule gives |alpha_d(x)[Dv(x + de)][P] - alpha_d(y)[Dv(y + de)][P]| <= c (H'_a S_v + S'_a H_v) |x - y|^alpha ||P||. Hence (H4) holds with a constant M2 independent of d. (H5) |w_d| <= S_v. (H6)-(H8) by steps 2-3. With M the max of these constants, the sibling dohr_eb_schauder_interior_estimate applied to (n, l, alpha, lam, M, 2R) gives C, independent of d, with ||Dw_d|| <= C and Dw_d alpha-Hoelder with C on B_R(xb).
5. The sibling dohr_eb_difference_quotient_limit (f := v, x0 := xb, e := e_k, rho := delta := R, M := C) shows that v_k := (x -> Dv(x) e_k) is C^1 on B_R(xb) with ||Dv_k|| <= C and Dv_k alpha-Hoelder with constant C there.
6. By P3, IsLocallyHolderCkα 1 alpha v_k U for every k. As v is C^1 on U, the sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((C) => (A), m = 1, E = R^l) gives IsLocallyHolderCkα 2 alpha v U.
Inductive step: m >= 2, the statement being known for m - 1 (for all data).
7. v is in C^{m,alpha}_loc(U), contained in C^2(U); every a_{rt}, Phi_r and every x -> a(x)[P][Q], x -> Phi(x)[P] is C^m, hence C^1, on U.
8. Differentiated system. Fix s, e := e_s, v_s := (x -> Dv(x) e_s), C^1 on U. Define for x in R^n the linear form Phi^(s)(x) := (fderiv R Phi x) e_s - (fderiv R (z -> a(z)[Dv(x)]) x) e_s, i.e. Phi^(s)(x)[P] = D_s(Phi(.)[P])(x) - D_s(a(.)[Dv(x)][P])(x) for x in U (since L is finite-dimensional, a map into L* or into L ->L L* whose components are C^1 on U is C^1 there, contDiffOn_clm_apply, and fderiv commutes with evaluation at P; Dv(x) is frozen in the second term). Claim: integral over U of a(x)[Dv_s(x)][Dzeta(x)] = integral over U of Phi^(s)(x)[Dzeta(x)] for zeta in C^1_c with tsupport in U. Proof: let Kz := tsupport zeta and h0 > 0 with Kz + closedBall(0, h0) contained in U. For 0 < |h| < h0 test the hypothesis with phi_h(x) := h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - he)) (C^1, tsupport in U) and translate the shifted part: - integral h^{-1}(a(y + he)[Dv(y + he)] - a(y)[Dv(y)])[Dzeta(y)] dy = - integral h^{-1}(Phi(y + he) - Phi(y))[Dzeta(y)] dy. As h -> 0, uniformly on Kz, h^{-1}(Phi(y + he) - Phi(y))[P] -> D_s(Phi(.)[P])(y) and h^{-1}(a(y + he)[Dv(y + he)] - a(y)[Dv(y)])[P] -> D_s(a(.)[Dv(y)][P])(y) + a(y)[D(Dv)(y) e][P] (product rule; uniform continuity of the derivatives on the compact Kz + closedBall(0, h0)), and D(Dv)(y) e = Dv_s(y) by symmetry of the second derivative of the C^2 map v (second_derivative_symmetric / ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt). 9. Regularity of the new data at order m - 1. (i) Legendre: same a and lam. (ii) For P, Q: x -> a(x)[P][Q] is C^m, so it is C^{m-1} with alpha-Hoelder (m-1)-th derivative on compacts (sibling dohr_eb_holder_of_contDiffOn_succ). (iv) v_s is in C^{m-1,alpha}_loc(U) (sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv, (A) => (C)).

subproblems.title: Induction step of the elliptic bootstrap: C^{m+1,alpha}_loc solution with C^{m,alpha}_loc right side is C^{m+2,alpha}_loc (m >= 1)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, 0 < alpha < 1, m >= 1, Psi : L(R^n, R^l) -> R C^infinity, lam > 0, eps in R with lam ||Q||^2 <= D^2 Psi(P)[Q][Q] whenever ||P|| <= eps, U open in R^n and u, g : R^n -> R^l with IsLocallyHolderCkα (m+1) alpha u U, ||Du|| <= eps on U, IsLocallyHolderCkα m alpha g U and integral over U of DPsi(Du)[Dphi] = - integral over U of <phi, g> for all C^1 compactly supported phi with tsupport in U. Then IsLocallyHolderCkα (m+2) alpha u U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → α < 1 → ∀ m : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → ∀ (Ψ : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) → ℝ) (lam ε : ℝ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (u g : Rn n → Rn ℓ), 0 < lam → IsOpen U → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) Ψ → (∀ P : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, ‖P‖ ≤ ε → ∀ Q : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, lam * ‖Q‖ ^ 2 ≤ fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Ψ) P Q Q) → IsLocallyHolderCkα (m + 1) α u U → (∀ x ∈ U, ‖fderiv ℝ u x‖ ≤ ε) → IsLocallyHolderCkα m α g U → (∀ φ : Rn n → Rn ℓ, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → tsupport φ ⊆ U → ∫ x in U, fderiv ℝ Ψ (fderiv ℝ u x) (fderiv ℝ φ x) = -∫ x in U, inner ℝ (φ x) (g x)) → IsLocallyHolderCkα (m + 2) α u U

Source: Step 5 of the parent proof (for 1 <= m: a = B o Du and the right side are C^{m,alpha}_loc; [GM] Theorem 5.20 applied to the differentiated system (D_k) gives D_k u in C^{m+1,alpha}_loc for every k, i.e. u in C^{m+2,alpha}_loc). Since u is already C^2 here, the system (D_k) is derived classically.
Notation: L = L(R^n, R^l), A(P) := DPsi(P), B(P)[Q][Q'] := fderiv R (fderiv R Psi) P Q Q', e_k = EuclideanSpace.single k 1.
0. Since m >= 1, IsLocallyHolderCkα (m+1) alpha u U gives u C^{m+1}, in particular C^2, on U.
1. Differentiated Euler-Lagrange system. For k in {1..n} put v_k := (x -> Du(x) e_k) (C^1 on U), a(x) := B(Du(x)) (the bilinear form fderiv R (fderiv R Psi) (fderiv R u x)) and Phi_k(x) := the linear form P -> <g(x), P e_k> (as a continuous linear map: (innerSL R (g x)) composed with evaluation at e_k). Claim: integral over U of a(x)[Dv_k(x)][Dzeta(x)] = integral over U of Phi_k(x)[Dzeta(x)] for every zeta in C^1_c with tsupport in U. Proof: let Kz := tsupport zeta and h0 > 0 with Kz + closedBall(0, h0) contained in U. For 0 < |h| < h0 test the hypothesis with phi_h(x) := h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - h e_k)) (C^1, compact support in U). Translating the shifted part (Lebesgue measure is translation invariant), integral A(Du(x))[Dphi_h(x)] dx = - integral h^{-1}(A(Du(y + h e_k)) - A(Du(y)))[Dzeta(y)] dy, while the right side is - integral <h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - h e_k)), g(x)> dx. As h -> 0: A o Du is C^1 on U (Psi C^2, u C^2), so h^{-1}(A(Du(y + h e_k)) - A(Du(y))) -> D(A o Du)(y) e_k = B(Du(y))[D(Du)(y) e_k] uniformly on Kz, and D(Du)(y) e_k = Dv_k(y) by symmetry of the second derivative of the C^2 map u; also h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - h e_k)) -> Dzeta(x) e_k uniformly. All integrands are continuous with support in the compact Kz + closedBall(0, h0), contained in U (they vanish on a neighbourhood of every point outside it), and bounded uniformly in h, so the limits pass under the integrals: - integral a[Dv_k][Dzeta] = - integral <Dzeta e_k, g> = - integral Phi_k[Dzeta], which is the claim.
2. Coefficient regularity. By the sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((A) => (B), E = R^l, level m), Du is C^m on U with D^m(Du) alpha-Hoelder on each compact subset of U. For fixed P, Q in L the scalar function h_PQ(R) := B(R)[P][Q] is C^infinity on L (Psi is C^infinity; h_PQ(R) = fderiv R (R' -> DPsi(R')[P]) R Q, a derivative of the smooth function R' -> DPsi(R')[P] followed by evaluation at Q), so h_PQ is C^m on the open set L and, by the sibling dohr_eb_holder_of_contDiffOn_succ (h_PQ is C^{m+1}), D^m h_PQ is alpha-Hoelder on compacts. The sibling dohr_eb_holder_comp (with 1 <= m, inner map Du : U -> L, outer map h_PQ, V = L) gives that x -> a(x)[P][Q] = h_PQ(Du(x)) is C^m on U with alpha-Hoelder m-th derivative on compacts.
3. Right side regularity. For fixed P, x -> Phi_k(x)[P] = lambda_P(g(x)) with lambda_P := <., P e_k> a continuous linear functional on R^l. On the open U, D^j(lambda_P o g) = lambda_P o D^j g (ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_left), so x -> Phi_k(x)[P] is C^m on U and ||D^m(lambda_P o g)(x) - D^m(lambda_P o g)(y)|| <= ||lambda_P|| ||D^m g(x) - D^m g(y)||, which is alpha-Hoelder on compacts because IsLocallyHolderCkα m alpha g U.
4. Legendre condition on U: for x in U, ||Du(x)|| <= eps, so a(x)[P][P] = B(Du(x))[P][P] >= lam ||P||^2.
5. v_k is in C^{m,alpha}_loc(U), i.e. IsLocallyHolderCkα m alpha v_k U: sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((A) => (C), level m) applied to u.
6. The sibling dohr_eb_linear_higher_regularity (with this m >= 1, U, lam, a, Phi_k, v_k; its hypotheses are steps 1-5) gives IsLocallyHolderCkα (m+1) alpha v_k U for every k.
7. u is C^1 on U and every v_k = (x -> fderiv R u x e_k) is in C^{m+1,alpha}_loc(U); the sibling dohr_eb_holder_succ_iff_fderiv ((C) => (A), level m+1) gives IsLocallyHolderCkα (m+2) alpha u U. QED
